key_insight: Combined CEL simulations and neural networks mapped HDPE friction stir welding quality, identifying 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating as optimal within the tested conditions.
engineering_relevance: Bottom preheating can reduce plunge loads and thermal gradients, helping engineers select more stable, defect-resistant HDPE welding conditions.
method: Developed a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model for temperature, axial force, material flow and defects.
Trained two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force responses.
Combined simulations and ANN predictions to map defective and defect-free process windows.
evidence_signal: Experimental validation supported the CEL predictions; ANNs achieved R² of 0.91–0.99, while 60 °C preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to about 1100 N.
watch_item: Predictive reliability beyond the tested process conditions remains unestablished, so new operating regimes require validation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
